primarySourcesInspected.title: National Institute of Korean Language. (n.d.). -시- [Korean Basic Dictionary entry].
primarySourcesInspected.locator: Entry -시-¹, senses 1–2: suffix elevating the subject of an action/state or a possessor/body-part subject; usage rules and examples.
primarySourcesInspected.finding: Official lexical grammar entry directly supports a subject honorific ending and its attachment; it does not establish Spanish translation equivalence or Guatemala-specific conventions. Referencia APA 7 candidata; apoyo parcial.

primarySourcesInspected.title: Kim, H. (2008). A study on the honorific expression in translated texts on the basis of the morph-tagged corpus. The Journal of Translation Studies, 9(4), 41–76. https://doi.org/10.15749/jts.2008.9.4.002
primarySourcesInspected.locator: Abstract and bibliographic record, lines 98–100 and 232–250: compares -시- and hearer-honorific endings in one-million-word translated and non-translated corpora.
primarySourcesInspected.finding: Shows translation corpora can differ in honorific morphology; this result is not a direct study of Korean-Spanish or Guatemalan equivalence. Referencia APA 7 candidata; apoyo parcial.

primarySourcesInspected.title: Real Academia Española & Asociación de Academias de la Lengua Española. (n.d.). Vos. Diccionario panhispánico de dudas.
primarySourcesInspected.locator: Entry “vos”, grammatical category and examples of second-person singular voseo; distinguishes regional usage and formal/informal treatment.
primarySourcesInspected.finding: Supports Spanish voseo as a regional second-person system; does not establish the variety-specific details of Guatemala without its cited examples. Referencia APA 7 candidata; apoyo parcial.
